newsitem.title: POLAND: AT LEAST 13 POLES FREEZE TO DEATH IN COLD WAVE.
newsitem.headline: AT LEAST 13 POLES FREEZE TO DEATH IN COLD WAVE.

text.p: The frozen bodies of three men have been found over the weekend, bringing to 13 Poland's death toll from a week-long cold spell that has sent temperatures as low as minus 37C., public television said on Sunday.
The body of a 44-year-old man, who was returning on foot from his mother's home several kilometres away, was found in a country lane in the the eastern province of Lublin.
Elsewhere in the same province, the body of 66-year-old Henryk S. was found on the edge of a forest with an empty vodka bottle at his side.
The weekend's third victim of the arctic cold wave was an elderly man whose body was discovered on a trash heap in the northern town of Olsztyn.

Since nearly all the victims had been intoxicated when overcome by the cold, the Polish media have been warning that alcohol not only does not fend off a chill but actually speeds up up the loss of body heat.
In Warsaw, a special ambulance has been collecting homeless people off the streets and taking them to special shelters for the duration of the cold spell. REUTER
